trialCategory.justificationOfLowIntervention: This clinical trial is considered a low-intervention clinical trial according to Article 2(2)(3) of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014. The detailed justification is as follows:  -	The investigational medicinal products (hormonal contraceptives) are already authorised.  -	According to the protocol, the investigational medicinal products are being used strictly in accordance with the terms of their respective marketing authorisations.  -	The additional diagnostic procedures (single venous blood draw of 17 mL for routine and specific laboratory testing) do not pose more than minimal additional risk or burden to the safety of the subjects compared to normal clinical practice.

trialObjective.mainObjective: This proposal focuses on evaluating thrombin generation and thrombosis risk in women on different forms of hormonal contraceptives, with a particular emphasis on modifiable risk factors that influence thrombosis risk. The study aims to identify actionable predictors for VTE risk, paving the way for personalized risk assessment and management strategies.To assess thrombin generation profiles and prethrombotic state in women using different formulations of hormonal contraceptives.To compare thrombin generation parameters between HC users and non-users.

secondaryObjectives.secondaryObjective: To identify and evaluate modifiable risk factors (e.g., smoking, BMI, physical activity, inflammation) influencing thrombin generation and thrombosis risk in HC users.

principalInclusionCriteria.principalInclusionCriteria: Current user of HC for at least 3 months/ Healthy non-users of HCs for at least 3 months as a control group

principalExclusionCriteria.principalExclusionCriteria: History of unexplained bleeding or hemophilia
Current use of anticoagulants/antiplatelets including NSAIDs in the past 10 days
Malignant disease within the past 5 years
Autoimmune disease influencing thrombotic risk (e.g. inflammatory bowel disease, SLE, etc)
Acute inflammation (including acute respiratory diseases, e.g. COVID-19, flu, RSV, etc)
Major surgery within the past 3 months

primaryEndPoints.endPoint: The normalized activated protein C sensitivity ratio (nAPCsr), determined by calibrated automated thrombography (CAT) assay, evaluated as the quantifiable difference in group means (expressed as absolute and percentage differences with 95% confidence intervals) between each hormonal contraceptive (HC) user subgroup and the healthy non-user control group.

secondaryEndPoints.endPoint: Evaluation of individual thrombin generation parameters, standard coagulation screening tests, routine laboratory parameters, and prothrombotic markers. Secondary outcomes also encompass markers of endothelial activation, fibrinolytic capacity, inflammatory cytokines/chemokines, and inherited thrombophilia screening. Furthermore, secondary analyses include the quantitative evaluation of the influence of modifiable risk factors on hemostatic balance and thrombosis risk across the study cohorts.
